A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CatVTON and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables. All pages were inspected, including v2's appendices; preliminary material and limitations moved from v1's main text can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original CatVTON benchmark results, qualitative outputs, efficiency comparisons and controlled ablations in Sections 4.4–4.6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds mask-free results, computational measurements, a text-conditioning ablation and appendix experiments with HunyuanDiT.

M1.justification: v2 adds an InstructPix2Pix-based mask-free model trained using synthetic pairs generated by the mask-based model, eliminating the supplied mask at inference. Sections 3.2–3.3 introduce its training and inference procedures. The revised equations and architecture diagram also place spatial concatenation before VAE encoding, whereas v1 encodes the images separately before concatenating their latents.

E1.justification: VITON-HD, DressCode, DeepFashion, garment categories and in-the-wild coverage remain. v2 extends evaluation to mask-free inference on the existing benchmarks and trains that variant with synthetic pairs derived from the retained datasets. This adds an input-requirement scenario without introducing a new application domain or benchmark.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark, efficiency and qualitative comparisons retain their external comparator sets. OutfitAnyone already appears in v1's in-the-wild comparison. The new profiling and DiT tables reuse subsets of existing comparators; newly cited methods such as BooW-VTON are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds batch-one inference profiling on an A100 at two resolutions, measuring GFLOPs, runtime and memory, and adds batch-one training throughput/memory measurements and new model configurations. The reported DeepFashion split changes from 13,098 total pairs including 1,896 test pairs to 13,098 training plus 1,896 test pairs. This is a revised stated split, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained module, DREAM and CFG ablations, v2 tests adding text conditioning and measures training-resource tradeoffs in Table 4. Appendix A.2.4 reports concatenation-direction and cross-direction inference tests, while A.4 tests transfer to HunyuanDiT. These substantially expand the architectural and transferability questions examined.

E5.justification: v2 Section 4.5 newly reports averaging inference times over 10 runs with identical input. v1 provides no corresponding repeated-run reporting. Neither version reports seeds, confidence intervals or variability for the image-quality benchmark scores.

E6.justification: The original Table 1 values remain unchanged under CatVTON (Inpainting). v2 adds mask-free results, including VITON-HD paired FID 5.888; DiT results, including paired FID 5.786 and SSIM 0.9118; text-conditioning results; and additional visual outputs. New profiling reports CatVTON inference times of 2.58 and 9.25 seconds at the two resolutions. These are additional configurations and measurements, not improvements to the retained original results.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the concatenated latent dimensions from eight channels to four channels with doubled spatial width and extends the formal input and denoising definitions to mask-free operation. The LDM and DREAM objectives are unchanged and relocated to Appendix A.1. Neither version introduces theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract's required-input claim broadens from person image, garment reference and mask in v1 to person and garment images alone in v2, supported by the new mask-free variant. This materially extends the central simplified-inference contribution. The spatial-concatenation, parameter-efficiency and generalization claims otherwise remain, with memory savings now explicitly quantified as 49%+.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets text-conditioning degradation, discusses concatenation-direction invariance and attributes incomplete DiT fitting to slower convergence. It also discusses applicability to GPUs below 8 GB while identifying smartphone deployment as unresolved. The VAE, mask-accuracy and pretrained-bias limitations are retained through relocation to Appendix A.5.

D1.justification: v2 adds InstructPix2Pix initialization and synthetic-pair preparation details, including parser cross-checks, convex hulls and pooling. Appendix A.2 specifies PyTorch 2.1.2, Diffusers, the server environment and 80 GB GPU memory. Existing principal training hyperparameters and the project access link remain.

R1.justification: Related work adds discussion of LoRA, PCDMs, InstantID and BooW-VTON, with new references supporting InstructPix2Pix and HunyuanDiT. MS-Diffusion and several general diffusion references are removed. These are targeted contextual updates; the central positioning around simplifying encoder-heavy virtual try-on systems remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methods and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting and condensation. v2 reorganizes the method subsections and moves preliminary material and limitations into an appendix alongside new implementation and experimental sections. Author, affiliation and conference-header information also changes.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a predominantly single-column conference layout, reorganizes the teaser, combines the structure/efficiency diagrams and merges the DREAM/CFG visualizations. It redraws the architecture, adds a mask-free training diagram, expands table structures and introduces profiling and DiT tables plus appendix comparison grids. These changes go well beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important practical gap in v1's simplified-inference claim by implementing and evaluating inference without a supplied mask. Its measured runtime and memory comparisons, text-conditioning ablation and implementation disclosures also substantially strengthen the efficiency argument beyond v1's parameter and model-loading comparisons. DiT training details remain sparse and quality-score uncertainty is still absent, but the practical extension and stronger validation provide a substantial overall improvement.
